answer: To resist sybils, a new agent must lock a refundable bond on a public stake ledge before its votes count. Identity then grows only as a vine of signed peer attestations across many epochs; isolated fresh keys have no vine and cannot swing consensus. When many newborn accounts suddenly emit the same echo of wording and timing, the protocol clusters them as one operator, slashes the shared bond, and zeros their weight until they re-earn independent history.
